comments: 1) Minimum particle size 0.010 um, width of bins = 0.132 in Ln space.  This width
corresponds to each bin diameter being about a factor of 1.14greater than the preceding one.
2) Row 53 contains the sums of the various columns
3) Columns A - D contain the results of sizing the particles with the TEM and binning them
4)  The main purpose of this sheet is to express the binned results in a reduced form
so that they can be compared with the lognormal distribution obtained by the moment
method
5) Column F contains the normalized distribution function.  This function has the desired
property that when integrated over dLnD gives a value of 1.0.
6)  Dmid in Channel is the geometric mean of the two channel boundaries.  Using this
value minimizes the effect of the finite channel width.  This is especially important
when the volume distribution is obtained from the number distribution.
7)  Column H and F are all that's needed for the number distribution.
8)  Column I and J are to determine Dg and Sigmag for comparison with the more detailed
analysis given in all data.  As mentioned above, the numbers agree within a few percent.
9) See note 6 regarding column L.  In this case we compute the square root of the product
of the particle volumes corresponding to the channel boundaries for the diameter.
10) Column N is the volume distribution function.  It also has the property that the
gration over dLnD is equal to 1.  In this case the normalization factor is the total volume.
11)  In terms of plotting the distribution functions, all one needs are H, J, and N.
